title: China Powers Ahead In Europe’s Car Recovery
text:
China Powers Ahead In Europe’s Car Recovery

August Gudmundsson

Gavekal Research | 23 Nov 2026

After years of subdued demand at home, European carmakers finally looked set for a recovery in 2026. Instead, Chinese brands are capturing most of the upswing, which is concentrated entirely in electric vehicles and hybrids. European producers are fighting back with cheaper, more advanced models, while import restrictions offer some protection. But neither can offset China’s enormous scale and cost advantages, especially as Chinese manufacturers increasingly localize production in Europe.This shift offers a silver lining for some European economies, as Chinese investment could offset declining production by European brands. But Europe is likely to capture less value added per car, while its domestic manufacturers remain under structural pressure. For equity investors, easing headwinds and the sector’s shrinking market weight offer some consolation, but a sustained turnaround remains elusive.
